text:
Artificial intelligence is rapidly changing the modern workplace. One of the most visible impacts is automation, where machines and software now handle repetitive tasks like data entry, scheduling, and basic customer service. This frees up employees to focus on more creative and strategic work. Meanwhile, productivity tools powered by AI are helping people write emails faster, analyze large sets of data, and even predict market trends.

However, AI is not simply replacing human workers; it is also creating new forms of human-AI collaboration. For example, doctors use AI to help read scans, while lawyers use it to review documents. This partnership means that job roles are changing. Instead of performing routine duties, many workers will need to learn how to supervise, interpret, and improve AI systems. While some jobs may disappear, many new ones will emerge, making adaptability a key skill for the future.
